compound_or_probe_identity: Reagent pair: (a) clemastine or benztropine, two M1 antagonist chemotypes also inhibiting EBP; (b) a structurally unrelated EBP inhibitor without M1 affinity (TASIN-1, or the CW9956/CW9009/CW3388 family: identity from the held ledger rows, in vitro only); (c) genetic control: Chrm1-null versus wild-type OPCs. No compound is nominated for use
pharmacology_sources: Hubler 2018 PMID 30046109 and Allimuthu 2019 PMID 30773481 (sterol/EBP, OPC monoculture, held ledger partial reads, not re-read); Mei 2016 Chrm1 knockouts (held summary R14-R18, primary not opened); Bohlen 2023 PMID 37068912 (clemastine, read this run); Ettle 2016 PMID 27059609 (abstract)
role: probe pair (reagent pair that separates two readings of one drug) with clemastine as the reusable drug comparator
known_in_neuron_driven_model: Not shown for a neuron-driven defect. Intrinsic-defect models only: Tcf4 het (EM g-ratio and uncompacted share, CAP N1/N2 ratio), Pdk1 icKO (marker, synapse, behaviour), alpha-synuclein (abstract). Tcf4 het total myelinated-axon density was NOT restored
transferred_from_injury_or_wild_type: wild-type neonatal mouse: markers up, callosal conduction velocity down (held E39-E40); adult lysolecithin and cuprizone acceleration (Deshmukh/Mei, held); neostigmine opposite (R52)
counter_evidence: (1) Chrm1-null OPCs differentiate about five-fold more and the drug effect is lost only there (held R14-R16) versus EBP inhibition, not M1 blockade, predicts the effect (held R33): unreconciled in held material. (2) Wild-type neonatal conduction fell. (3) Total myelinated axon density not restored in Tcf4 het (V01). (4) Uninjured myelin unchanged by OPC Chrm1 deletion (R17)
comparator_for_functional_outcome: sheath structure in the dish (MBP+ internodes per axon length and internode length, with a marker level beside it); conduction not measurable in the dish: next level is a slice or callosal CAP arm, and for a wild-type neuron condition the adverse-effect arm
control_that_separates_mechanism: (a) EBP inhibitor without M1 affinity in Chrm1-null OPCs (if it still acts, the sterol route works without M1); (b) clemastine/benztropine in Chrm1-null OPCs (loss of effect = M1 route; persistence = sterol route); (c) sterol profiling (zymostenol, zymosterol) as target engagement, not yet shown in a co-culture
two_chemotypes_same_target_shown: two chemotypes on one target: shown for EBP in OPC monoculture (clemastine, benztropine, tamoxifen, U50488 and independent scaffolds) by held ledger rows; NOT shown to be the only route for clemastine because the Chrm1 genetic result disagrees. Not assumed
marker_reflects_function_shown: not shown. Hubler: MBP+ formation and microfibre ensheathment in vitro; Tcf4 het: marker and EM and CAP all moved in the same direction (intrinsic defect); wild-type neonatal: marker and conduction diverged
adult_injury_label_and_transfer: Mixed: adult-injury evidence (lysolecithin, cuprizone, hypoxia) for most compounds; the transfer to development is not established (neonatal clemastine impaired conduction in wild type) and is stated as such

compound_or_probe_identity: Lipid and substrate supply arm: cholesterol and fatty-acid enrichment (diet-level in vivo evidence only) and ketone bodies as axonal substrate. Dish reagents (cholesterol carrier, fatty-acid mix, beta-hydroxybutyrate) are NOT verified in any source read for this co-culture
pharmacology_sources: Camargo 2017 PMID 28549068 (read this run: astrocyte-SCAP, HFD from E15, conduction); Dietary KD Plp1tgB PMID 30919030 (read this run); SLC44A1 citicoline abstract PMID 41317319; aspartoacylase abstract PMID 27717881 (genetic)
role: proposal without an interpretable reagent in the dish (the in vivo diet result is a control for the supply explanation; the dish reagent must first be shown to enter myelin membrane there)
known_in_neuron_driven_model: Not tested with a neuron-driven defect. Defect outside the oligodendrocyte but in the astrocyte: HFD rescued myelination (text) and callosal fast-wave presence (5 to 50 percent of slices). KD: conduction gain exceeded myelination gain in an oligodendrocyte-intrinsic model
transferred_from_injury_or_wild_type: oligodendrocyte-intrinsic models (PLP overexpression, SLC44A1, ASPA) and cuprizone remyelination (KD)
counter_evidence: Cholesterol with an intact barrier gave no major benefit in two PMD patients and little in the BBB-intact mouse; HFD rescue is partial; exposure began at E15 (prevention), and a delay in lipid synthesis can normalise by itself with age (CNP-SCAP P20 to P120)
comparator_for_functional_outcome: callosal or optic nerve CAP and EM g-ratio on diet versus control; in the dish, internode number and length with the supply arm in both neuron genotypes
control_that_separates_mechanism: a wild-type neuron condition and a vehicle carrier control; tracer lipid (plant sterol or labelled cholesterol) in myelin as engagement (shown in vivo: campesterol/sitosterol in myelin)
two_chemotypes_same_target_shown: not applicable to chemotypes; cholesterol versus ketone bodies act on different aspects (the KD paper: cholesterol did not reverse axonal mitochondrial enlargement, KD did)
marker_reflects_function_shown: not shown: CAP gain exceeded myelination gain in KD; oligodendrocyte counts were normal with thin myelin in the astrocyte model
adult_injury_label_and_transfer: Developmental in vivo diets; adult cuprizone arm only for KD. Transfer to neuron-driven hypomyelination not established
